title: Customer Breadcrumb Collection — micro-themes & prioritized asks
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This doc is a lightweight, messy roll-up of small recurring signals we keep seeing in CS calls and support threads (Apr–May 2028).
Goal: 1) surface micro-themes product/eng can act on in 1–8 weeks, 2) provide concise asks and suggested next steps, 3) note risk flags customers keep bringing up.

How to read: these are breadcrumbs — not a full synthesis. If something looks high-impact, flag for a proper VOC deep-dive.

Topline micro-themes (ranked by frequency in last 6 weeks):
1) Cost visibility by request-phase (token-level/phase breakouts) — frequent and emotive.
   - What customers say: "We can show overall cost per API call, but not how much the prompt vs generated tokens cost us, or where the pricing spikes happen across retries/batched requests."
   - Typical customer: mid-market SaaS, usage-based product teams with tight unit economics.
   - Impact: blockers to converting high-volume customers and to internal finance reconciliation.
   - Suggested quick-win: expose per-request breakdown: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_hits, model_variant_used. 2–3 week dev + small UI change in Console usage page.

2) Predictable fallback behavior & visibility for model rollouts
   - Signal: customers with strict latency/quality SLOs fear silent fallback to cheaper variants (esp during Dedicated autoscaling events).
   - Quote: "We had a canary roll and saw weird hallucinations; we couldn't tell whether traffic was routed to the old model or a fallback variant."
   - Short ask: add explicit per-request headers/logs (or Console trace) that record model_variant and routing_reason. Make it easy to filter traces where routing_reason != expected. 3–6 week.

3) More granular autoscale burst controls for Dedicated customers
   - Signal: customers want bounded burst capacity for short spikes without committing to higher reserved capacity.
   - Workaround many use: developer-level throttles + client-side exponential backoff, but it's fragile.
   - Ask: a per-tenant "short-term burst reserve" knob (configurable minutes & tp/s) + cost-preview. Proof-of-concept could reuse existing burst pool code path. 6–10 weeks.

4) Better debugging ergonomics around KV/prefix caching
   - Signal: teams using conversation-heavy workflows struggle to reason about cache consistency and evictions. They ask for: cache diagnostics, peek cache contents/keys in dev mode, and cache-miss attribution.
   - Quick idea: add an opt-in dev header that returns cache_hit=true/false + small KV key sample in logs (redacted). 2–4 weeks.

5) Function/tool-calling debug trace (end-to-end)
   - Signal: customers integrating with tools (internal APIs, DB calls) want a step-by-step trace showing which function was called, input payload, which model response triggered it, and latency breakdown.
   - Risk: PII/exfiltration concerns — needs redaction config.
   - Ask: add a function-call trace mode in Console + SDK that captures call sequences (redaction selectable). 4–8 weeks.

Representative customer quotes (raw excerpts):
- "We need to show finance a breakdown or we won't get sign-off for the next quarter. Right now it's a lump-sum cost and can't tie to features." — fintech startup, $X/mo spend.
- "During a traffic surge our latency spiked and quality dropped. Took us a while to realize it was falling back to a 7B variant." — digital assistant platform.
- "We want a dev-mode where I can see what the KV cache currently has so I can debug conversation state. Right now it's black box." — CX automation partner.

Small prioritized asks (immediate -> near-term):
- A1 (Quick Win, 2 weeks): Add prompt/completion token split to the request logs & Console usage table. Small backend + minor UI column. Owner: product-hosted-api + observability.
- A2 (Quick Win, 2–3 weeks): Add model_variant used metadata in the request trace (log field + SDK/HTTP response header). Owner: serving-runtime + SDK team.
- A3 (Short Project, 4–6 weeks): Opt-in cache-debug header for dev environments that returns cache_hit flag and evicted_key_sample (redacted). Owner: serving-runtime.

Mid-term / higher effort asks (6–12 weeks):
- B1: Dedicated: configurable burst reserve UI & price-preview. Needs eng infra, billing, legal review.
- B2: End-to-end function-call trace mode with redaction policy & storage retention controls. Requires console UI work + storage planning.

Risk flags (what customers repeatedly warn about):
- Silent quality regressions during model rollouts (customer trust hit if not surfaced).
- Billing disputes due to opaque cost attribution (finance teams unhappy).
- Security/privacy: customers want assurance that debug/capture modes can be fully disabled for Private deployments.

Open questions / unknowns we should validate:
- How many active paying customers would convert to higher commitment if we shipped burst-reserve vs how many would just use it temporarily? (ask sales for a short list of 8 accounts to run quick interviews).
- For cost-breakdown exposure, do we need legal review around showing per-token cost if customers resell features? (pull in billing/legal).
- For cache-debug: what's safe to show in shared logs without violating customer PII? We need SRE/security guidance on automated redaction heuristics.

Suggested next steps / owner suggestions (very pragmatic):
1) Product + CS quick sync (30m) — get buy-in on A1/A2 prioritization. Owner: Amelia.
2) Triage call with serving-runtime + observability (1h) to scope effort for A2 + A3. Owner: Diego.
3) Pull 6-week pilot list of customers for short interviews (sales + CSMs provide list). Owner: Priya.
4) Create 2-line PRD for burst-reserve (B1) to validate cross-functional feasibility with billing and infra. Owner: product-dedicated.

Notes / raw capture (snippets from threads):
- "If we could flag a per-request header that says model=redwood-1-steer-16k and routing=canary, I can automate our alerting rules." — customer thread 2028-05-02.
- "We had a monthly bill spike and couldn't reconcile tokens due to retries from clients during early-hours maintenance." — support ticket CS-2028-1140.

Todo (this doc):
- [ ] Run the A1 engineering feasibility check (observability team)  — due 2028-05-18.
- [ ] Compile top 8 customers for short interviews about burst-reserve — due 2028-05-20.
- [ ] Draft PRD for model_variant trace header — due 2028-05-24.

Misc (notes to self):
- Keep the term 'breadcrumbs' when we want fast-rolling micro-features; keeps conversations small.
- This has overlap with "voice-of-customer-2028" confluence page — don't duplicate; use this doc for tactical asks only.

If you want a one-pager for exec: I can compress to 1 slide with asks A1/A2 and customer quotes — ping me.

-- Amelia
